title: Judge Sheets — predictive spreadsheet columns
one_liner: A Sheets-lookalike grid where typing a column header ("Urgency", "Refund risk?") fills the whole column with semantic judgments in seconds.
what_it_does: The page opens a spreadsheet with two sheets. Reviews holds 300 synthetic product reviews. Leads holds 150 synthetic inbound B2B messages. Two columns ship pre-predicted: Sentiment on Reviews and Intent on Leads. The user clicks an empty header cell to the right of the text column and types a header such as "Urgency". After 120 ms of quiet, one classify request reads the header plus three sample rows and picks one of 14 prediction schemas. A chip under the cell shows the schema, its probability and the measured latency. On Enter the column fills with =JUDGE / =PICK / =RATE formulas for every data row, and the engine batches the pending judgments to the API. Cells render as "Yes · 97%" with red/green tint, a category label with confidence tint, or a level label on a red-to-green scale. A "Column predicted" card shows rows done, wall time, median and p95 latency, rows per second, and the "one LLM prompt per cell" baseline with a speedup multiple. Keep commits the column, Undo clears it, a dropdown re-interprets the header with another schema. Summary blocks (COUNT, AVERAGE, COUNTIF) recalculate as answers land. Formula bar, fill handle, Ctrl+Shift+D and column resize all work.

jev_questions.instructions: A spreadsheet user typed this column header above a column of free text. Which kind of prediction do they want in that column?
options: sentiment / how positive or negative the text is
urgency / how quickly someone needs to follow up
topic / category of a product review
intent of an inbound message / what the sender wants
buying intent / how likely the sender is to purchase
priority / severity for a support or ops team
star rating the author would give (1 to 5)
whether the text reports a defect, damage or malfunction
whether the author would recommend the product
whether the author is likely to return the product or ask for a refund
whether the message is spam or unrelated
some other yes/no question (the header itself is the question)
some other quality rated low to high (the header names the quality)

jev_questions.instructions: What is the main topic of this text?
This is an inbound message to a B2B software company. What does the sender want?
How strong is the sender's intent to purchase our product?
What is the emotional tone of the writer?
How severe is the problem described, from a support team's point of view?

Does the text report a defect, damage or malfunction of the product itself?
Would the author recommend the product to others?
Is the author likely to return the product or ask for a refund?
Is this message spam, a scam, or unrelated to the business?
Answer this question about the text: {header}  (a '?' is appended when the header lacks one)

request_cadence: Header chip: one choice request per header edit after a 120 ms debounce (in-flight request aborted on the next keystroke). Column fill: one systemone request per distinct source text with every pending question for that text fanned out inside it, so 300 rows = 300 requests, run through a 12-lane pool on the proxy. Workbook open: 450 requests (two seeded columns). Cache by (kind, text, instructions, options) makes re-interpretation free.

{"texts":[...],"statement":"The author is likely to return the product or ask for a refund.","when_true":"Mentions returning it, wanting money back, or a serious defect with anger.","when_false":"Is satisfied, or only mentions a minor gripe that is not a deal-breaker."}

{"texts":[...lead messages],"statement":"This message is spam, a scam or unrelated to the business.","when_true":"Unsolicited SEO, backlink, traffic, offshore development or domain listing offers.","when_false":"A real question about pricing, demos, support, partnership or jobs."}
{"texts":[...],"statement":"{header rewritten as a declarative}"}  e.g. header "Mentions a competitor?" -> {"statement":"The text mentions a competitor."}
dm1_mapping.notes: Client rewrite rule: strip trailing '?', if header starts with a verb (Mentions/Asks/Is/Has/Wants...) prefix 'The text ' and lower-case the first letter; otherwise 'The text is about {header}.' No hints. Shown in the card so the user can edit the statement before Keep.

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: {"texts":[...],"scale":["no {header} at all","low {header}","medium {header}","high {header}","very high {header}"]}  e.g. header "Enthusiasm" -> ["no enthusiasm at all","low enthusiasm","medium enthusiasm","high enthusiasm","very high enthusiasm"]

browser_plan: Keep the app as a Vite/React island in the demos repo at /sheets. Copy src/engine, src/data, src/ui/Grid, Chrome, icons, format and store.ts as-is. Replace src/styles.css tokens with the milliseconds.ai site tokens from ~/projects/cloudraker-spring-2026 (fonts, colors, radius); keep the grid geometry. Drop server/* except pool.ts. Proxy: one Cloudflare Worker (or the demos site's existing /api proxy) exposing POST /api/dm1/:route that forwards the JSON body to https://api.milliseconds.ai/v1/decision-machine-1/:route with the bearer key from a secret, passes back status, body and the x-inference-ms / x-input-tokens headers. Rewrite src/lib/predict.ts: keep SCHEMAS but store a dm1 body builder per schema (route + statement/hints, labels or scale) and the display mapping above; replace classifyIntent with one POST /api/dm1/classify. Rewrite src/lib/jevClient.ts as dm1Client.ts: batchSpecs now groups pending specs by question key (kind + instructions + options) instead of by text, then slices each group into chunks of 32 texts; each chunk is one request with texts:[...]. 300 rows = 10 requests, 450 rows on open = 15 requests. A single client-side token bucket allows 2 requests per second (500 ms spacing) with 4 in flight max; the header chip request bypasses the queue but still counts. On 429 read Retry-After (default 2 s), pause the bucket, show 'Rate limited, resuming in Ns' in the card and footer, and requeue the chunk; after 3 failed attempts write #RATE into the cells and offer Retry in the card. Latency per request = x-inference-ms; p50/p95/rows-per-s stats stay as before. Cache key = (route, text, body-without-texts) so re-interpreting a header stays free. Yes-no answers map to JUDGE values (probability), classify to PICK values (label, scores), rate to RATE values (score*(levels-1), level). Add a 'How it works' drawer under the card showing the exact JSON body sent for the current column, a curl line, and a link to the docs.
risks: Free-form 'Yes / no' schema depends on rewriting a header question into a declarative statement; the heuristic will misfire on odd headers, so expose the statement for editing before Keep.
Free-form 'Low / high' scale injects the header into level descriptions; some headers read poorly and quality may drop versus the fixed schemas.
Rate scores are 0..1 weighted position, not 0..N expected level; summary formulas that threshold at 1.5 and 2.5 need the score*(N-1) conversion applied consistently.

Org-wide 200 req/min limit is shared across all demo pages and visitors; workbook open costs 15 requests per visitor, so consider lazy-predicting the seeded columns only when a sheet is visible, or shipping the seeded columns as cached values.
Batching by question instead of by text means a review column of 3 predicted columns costs 3x the requests of Jev's fan-out; still 30 requests for 300 rows, under the budget.
The 'one LLM prompt per cell' baseline (4 s per cell) is a marketing number; keep it labelled as an assumption.
The intent classifier over 14 described labels was tuned for Jev choice; classify may need label descriptions rebalanced so 'Yes / no' and 'Low / high' do not win over the specific schemas.
Formula engine tests reference JUDGE/PICK/RATE names and the JevSpec shape; keep the names so tests and the formula bar stay meaningful.
